top.line: Anthropic's five primitives for always-on agents, beside the around 250 named agents six of us ran at Web Summit.
top.para: Same five boxes, different material; where we agree, where we were wrong, and the next problems a team meets.

in-short.line: The post, the five primitives, our version, agreement, the next problems, and the spirit of it.

scale.line: For readers new here: six people, around 250 named agents, 224 sessions, more than 60 at once, about 20,000 commits.
scale.para: A collage of 24 sites and apps, the numbers, the ten days in order, and what came before in October.

post.line: Agents that mostly sleep, wake on an event, work and save: inbox, timers, memory, permissions, outbox.
post.para: Written for one agent per user, from database tables and workers.

mapping.line: We built the same five from git, files, vaults and keys.
mapping.para: Inbox lanes sealed to keys, scheduled wakes, the repository as memory, keys and signed commits, the site as outbox.

agree.line: Inbox as source of truth, lean memory, and start quiet, the last learned by getting it wrong.
agree.para: 106 hand-overs on one site; a newsroom that ran nine days on "nothing new"; 98.7% cache reads.

next.line: Once there are many: agents starting agents, identity, stopping, many humans, seeing it, governance.
next.para: A stop is an event, only as fast as the timers: 5 to 33 minutes.

owe.line: We run on Claude Code: its credential proxy and auto mode protected our agents.
owe.para: Some of our boxes were rougher; the next version should borrow the post's.

start.line: Where to go next: the earlier articles to read first, in order.
start.para: The map, the operating system, how we work, inboxes and keys, speed, stopping, governance, and beyond code.

limits.line: A comparison, not a contest; our figures from our records; not reviewed by Anthropic.

sources.line: William Hu's post and our repositories, as summarised in the Ten days series.
sources.para: With links to the inbox, keys, secrets and stop button articles.
